decisions.reason: Caption styling is an independent requirement, and its same-message scope extension to monthly production is already represented.
The clean-editing scope change does not alter the independently defined teaching-moment requirement; its new audience-comprehension rule is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
The editing-style scope change does not alter source selection, and the B-roll and long-form-video source requirements are already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
The candidate already requires 45-to-60-second clips in monthly production, so the source message only restates its current duration state.
Requiring clean editing for monthly clips does not necessarily extend the distinct strong-or-impactful-moment selection requirement beyond its trial scope.
The candidate already requires client approval before publication; the source message does not change its approval authority or rejection handling.
The source message's batch, deadline, folder, access, and submission-channel changes are already fully represented by a same-message MODIFY.
A five-clip production batch does not modify or necessarily resume the deferred monthly quota of 100 approved clips.
Applying clean editing standards to monthly clips does not change the Lead Clipper pathway, compensation, training focus, or responsibilities.
The five clips requested in the source message are described as the first live production batch, not as a change to the completed qualification process.
The Friday publication schedule and late-delivery policy are already represented by a same-message MODIFY, while the clean-editing scope change adds nothing further.
